title: Certify raw Gaussian interiors against shared rounded references
body:
The Gaussian caller needs raw interior blocks of one fixed rounded
reference. I construct that reference and connect its constant-phase
restrictions to the complete forward circuit and the inverse of the
same stored program.

I retain the source's nearest-up phase geometry, original period cut
and different hole rules. Narrow completion adds identity hole
coordinates; broad completion keeps Gaussian outputs at hole rows
and adds identity hole columns. I prepare positive narrow weights
and one shared truncated kernel. For broad coefficients I choose a
fixed entrywise reference and prove its comparison; I do not identify
it with the older factorwise-rounded broad matrix.

For a declared dyadic cap, radius and target, `Reference.for_cap`
chooses global cutoffs and coefficient precision before any block
requests. I derive row and column error bounds including periodic
aliases, then compute a narrow row-gap certificate for that same
reference. A positive gap gives principal-inverse bounds in the
original circular coordinates. Coordinate queries and capped pages
do not enumerate the full axis.

I implement the anchored broad and narrow diagonal factors around
the completed normalized `Tsec`/`full_plan` circuit. I store positive
coefficients once and invert those same values for the reverse program.
I pay weight setup, kernel truncation, diagonal quantization, circuit
rounding and the fixed-reference inverse comparison.

For target `2^-t`, input radius `R`, incoming grid `F0`, normalized
scale `c` and anchored exponent range `Fg`, the online width is

`O(F0 + t + log n + log R + 1/c + Fg + log alpha)`.

Full-cell weights remain offline setup objects at
`O(entry_bits + alpha²/theta)` bits. Under the later caller's parameter
range, I obtain the retained `O(p² log p)` setup order and
`O(sqrt(p log p))` broad bandwidth. The raw wrapper adds two scalar
layers and `2n` gates. I reject an insufficient fixed reference or a
period too short for the allocated cutoff.

Evidence:

- I check 2,178 entries across two complete 33-by-33 references, using
  three explicit windings and analytic remaining-tail bounds. I check
  both induced norms, actual row gaps, a principal inverse crossing a
  phase boundary and a hole, shared overlapping pages and retained cuts.
- Six raw-circuit fixtures execute 1,086 gates and 26 rounded states.
  I include positive/negative cell centers, broad/narrow maps and a
  512-bit incoming vector.
- Seventeen controls cover setup underflow, insufficient reference
  precision/tails, stale pages, hole completion and inverse-wrapper order.
  Increasing reference precision changes the reference while retaining
  the same online program.
- I query a capped window on a source axis of size `10^20+1` without
  enumerating the axis. This is a local address/producer check.
- Raw scientific receipt:
  `f9c2bfc6b61ca8a52c403d912d2f687beb3641955cec71d3879ab017b067d6f7`.

I preserve the five earlier scientific receipts. I run full, normalized
and raw verification sequentially in the two final manifest slots,
retaining eight commands and a total timeout budget of 1,200 seconds.
The interval comparisons share Mason Hale's declared backend; reviewers
must assess the universal arguments separately from the finite receipts.

At head `c9db4069d59bfad26a15fe000b91cc3a058684e5`, I passed the
54-file committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export
integrity check. All eight registered and Git-free commands pass;
all 55 exported files stayed unchanged. The final combined commands
took 32.439 and 33.041 seconds in the export.
Archive SHA256: `136d7dd95fc29b427afa7c7f55a140537a8561a971bdc1ef12a341a5989f5234`;
receipt SHA256: `129c6f4fbdd9ccedd3e232023456fead49ce55e2ae767abb0c4a51119b7c565a`.
I matched all twelve successful
[hosted records](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39477979592)
to the export, including all six scientific digests and the unchanged-input
step. Test merge `ebc06734b5645c1eb8e8f5a780ca289b3147c8ae` has the exact
base/head parents and publication tree `7b8c6b4149fe23de7b79a8f9370f0da972ed704d`.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/rational-unitary-fft
```

I start from canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`,
priority revision 7. I preserve normalized revision
`66b95cc916552f487203be14fd99a7aea0bdd78e` and its
[hosted evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39470174495),
along with earlier completed revisions.
[Discussion4202](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4202)
records the source pins, expansion decision and overlap coverage.
Before publication I refreshed unchanged main, checked 12 newer PR
records and 5/815 hub comments, and read the new scalar-audit handoff.

The block admission checks constant phase, dyadic size and the original
cut. I leave the actual separated carve, complete Schur/boundary program,
physical coefficient delivery, tensor layout and tape costs open.
The broad boundary factor requires application; the narrow inverse
caller requires its separate solve. I leave the selected frontier unchanged.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
I credit Vlado Vojdanovski for phase-cell references and circuits;
Jeremy Kothe/IdeaOuter for shifted identities; Mason Hale for interval
arithmetic and earlier Gaussian execution; Chafik Boukhalfa for phases
and fine-prime setup work; and Cinna Davis for the later caller.
I retain ToikY's distinct Schur theorem and James Reed's scoped audit
at the earlier `fdcdc269` head. ToikY's
[PR4220](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4220),
head `5cf23ba47a28b78a98eb0665177b5030e65c01b9`, separately audits the
scalar enclosure and precision rules at normalized source `66b95cc916`.
Its author reports 128 independent intervals covering 186 source observations;
the audit excludes the full circuit, matrix-inverse theorem and this raw
extension. Internal agents belong to our author process.
